title: Granite Coast House
summary: A sheltered terrace runs the length of the living rooms. The lower floor opens towards fynbos and granite, while the upper bedrooms face the Atlantic. A separate study and level entry on the arrival floor suit extended stays. Coastal exposure sets the maintenance budget.
alt: AI-generated Cape Peninsula villa with limestone walls, timber screens and a pool overlooking the Atlantic.

sections.title: Architecture and title
sections.body: The model assumes a single full-title residential erf in the City of Cape Town. The surface areas are stated separately so terraces and garages cannot inflate the internal price per square metre.
rows: Full title. Owner occupation or one long residential lease. Confirm deed, servitudes, zoning and any consent with the conveyancer and municipality.
480 m² internal (5,167 sq ft), 84 m² terraces (904 sq ft), 54 m² garage (581 sq ft). Site 1,600 m² (17,222 sq ft). Garage and terraces excluded from 480 m².
Five bedrooms, four en suites, family bathroom, guest WC, separate study, utility, double garage and two off-street spaces.

Reinforced concrete frame, masonry infill, stone cladding, low-slope membrane roof, municipal utilities and battery-backed essential circuits. Step-free entrance on the arrival floor. Stair access between levels.
Sea-facing living terrace with a wind-screened court behind. Marine corrosion, waterproofing, slope drainage and access after storms require inspection.
Land, improvements and specified fixed fittings. Furniture, movable art and business goodwill excluded. Vacant possession assumed. No booking or letting history accompanies the example.

sections.title: What the inspection would test
sections.body: This mock inspection summary shows how an exception changes the buyer’s budget. Only a coordinated structural inspection and approved drawings could establish the actual condition and areas.
rows: Illustrative deed schedule identifies one erf. Survey diagram, servitudes and municipal plan reconciliation remain open. Compare the pool and terrace footprint against stamped plans.
Example visual finding: moisture staining at one terrace threshold. Trace the water path, open a test area with consent and obtain two scoped repair quotations.
Example visual finding: surface corrosion on exposed fixings. Obtain a façade specialist’s schedule. Request roof membrane, joinery and pool-service records.
Engineer to inspect retaining walls and drainage. Conveyancer to obtain clearances and confirm the occupation, compliance certificate and disclosure documents applicable to this transfer.
R220,000 placeholder for waterproofing, drainage and corroded hardware. Update after a measured survey.

sections.title: Rental underwriting
sections.body: A long-lease scenario uses monthly rent of R160,000 and 10% economic vacancy. There is no executed lease or collected income. Operating expenses exclude finance, income tax, capital expenditure and acquisition costs.
rows: R160,000 × 12 = R1,920,000 / year. Gross scheduled yield 6.00% of the R32m price.
R192,000 vacancy allowance. Effective gross income R1,728,000.
Rates R204,000 + insurance R72,000 + repairs R156,000 + garden and pool R108,000 + management R96,000 = R636,000.
R1,728,000 − R636,000 = R1,092,000. Scenario cap rate 3.41% on price.
At 5%, 10% and 20% vacancy, fixed-cost NOI equals R1,188,000, R1,092,000 and R900,000. Yield on price is 3.71%, 3.41% and 2.81%.
Capitalising R1,092,000 at assumed 3.0%, 3.5% and 4.0% implies R36.40m, R31.20m and R27.30m. These scenarios require local achieved sales and signed lease evidence before pricing a real instruction.

sections.title: Acquisition cost
sections.body: This cash-purchase scenario assumes the South African transfer-duty route at R32m and the tariff effective 1 April 2026. Ask the conveyancer to establish whether the transaction instead attracts VAT and whether the stated price includes it.
rows: R180,000 conveyancing, registration and disbursements + R60,000 due diligence + R220,000 initial works. These gross cash allowances require current quotations.
R36,131,156. NOI of R1,092,000 gives 3.02% on all-in cash cost before financing or income tax. A deposit paid towards the price is credited once.

sections.title: Buyer and seller routes
sections.body: The property remains in South Africa. The purchaser’s residence, funding route and legal identity determine additional checks.
rows: Confirm identity and source of funds through the conveyancer, inspect title and plans, agree finance and inspection conditions, obtain a duty assessment, sign transfer documents, then confirm Deeds Office registration.

Arrange the inward transfer with a South African authorised dealer, retain inward-remittance evidence and obtain written borrowing capacity. Test the relevant exchange-control funding ratio against the buyer and purpose. Have the bank confirm timing and eventual remittance evidence.

Provide title, bond cancellation details, approved plans, disclosure and certificates. Agree responsibility for rates, inspection exceptions and occupation. Reconcile tax, costs and net proceeds on the conveyancer’s completion statement.

Where section 35A applies above R2m, statutory withholding on the full price is 7.5% for an individual, 10% for a company and 15% for a trust, subject to a SARS directive. On R32m, the individual example is R2.4m advance withholding. The final tax follows assessment.
Release keys at the agreed contractual milestone. Record meter readings, fittings inventory and evidence of cleared settlement. Obtain local written advice before relying on the lease scenario.

example_status: Fictional asset. Prices, specifications, operating assumptions and inspection notes are illustrative. AI-generated editorial imagery. No asset is being offered for sale.
